========================================================================
BEGIN FROZEN PRE-REGISTRATION
Title : p-scaling of the sub-Rayleigh mean-|U| deficit of the additive
        character on E: y^2 = x^3 + 7  (enumerable model curves only)
Status: FROZEN, pre-data. No D(p) value has been computed.
Author agent: experiment-designer
Date  : 2026-08-04
========================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. SCOPE BANNER  (read first, applies to every number this spec produces)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is a SCALING LAW OF A MODEL OBJECT. E: y^2 = x^3+7 is enumerated over
SMALL primes p (151 .. 12043). NOTHING here transfers to cryptographic p.
"Persistent" will mean "persistent across the enumerable model range under
the fitted functional form" and NEVER a statement about p ~ 2^256.
Extrapolating any fitted law to cryptographic scale is FORBIDDEN as a
conclusion of this experiment. j-invariant is 0 (CM by Z[zeta_3]); results
are specific to this curve family and to a_0 = 1 (with a stated
all-character secondary).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. OBJECT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Fix p = 1 mod 6 with E(F_p) CYCLIC of order n; G a canonical generator
(rule below). Points P_d = [d]G, d = 1..n-1, exhaust the non-identity group.
For (b,c) in F_p x F_p and a_0 = 1:

   U(b,c) = sum_{d=1}^{n-1} zeta_n^{a_0 d} * e_p( b*x_{P_d} + c*y_{P_d} )
   zeta_n = e^{2*pi*i/n},  e_p(k) = e^{2*pi*i*k/p}.

OBJECT of measurement: the l1 concentration functional
   M[g]  =  (1/p^2) * sum_{b,c} |U_g(b,c)|,
   where U_g uses weight g(d) in place of zeta_n^{a_0 d}.
We measure whether the CHARACTER weight g(d)=zeta_n^{a_0 d} yields a
systematically SMALLER M than random unit-phase weights, and how that gap
scales in p. M is a direct functional of the transform U, not a proxy.

TAUTOLOGY / SHARED-CONSTRUCTION CHECK.
 - l2 is FORCED and therefore cannot be the statistic:
     sum_{b,c} |U_g(b,c)|^2 = p^2 * sum_d |g(d)|^2 = p^2 (n-1)
   EXACTLY for the character AND for every unit-phase g (a genuine integer
   identity: sum_{b,c} e_p(b*dx + c*dy) = p^2 * [dx=0 & dy=0], points
   distinct). Hence any l2-normalized statistic is identical across targets
   and is excluded by construction.
 - The character weight and the null weight SHARE the point set and the
   transform; they differ ONLY in g(d). The one structure they also share
   by force is the Hermitian symmetry g(n-d)=conj(g(d)) (since
   zeta_n^{a_0(n-d)} = conj(zeta_n^{a_0 d})). That shared symmetry is a
   tautology risk for the NULL and is neutralized in Sec.3 (matched null).
 - M[character] is a single deterministic number for (p,G,a_0); it is not
   an average over an ensemble that shares construction with the null.
   No tautology remains once the null carries the Hermitian symmetry.

CANONICAL GENERATOR RULE (deterministic, pre-committed).
 G = the affine point (x,y), 0<=x,y<p, minimal in (x, then y), whose order
 is n (generates E). Order verified by [n/l]G != O for every prime l | n.
 d -> P_d=[d]G fixes the labeling; x_d,y_d are exact integers in [0,p).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. STATISTIC  (exactly one primary per-prime statistic; one pooled slope)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Per-prime deficit (the object):
   M_char(p)   = M[ zeta_n^{a_0 (.)} ]                       (deterministic)
   For k=1..K(p) matched-null draws g^(k) (Sec.3): M_k = M[g^(k)].
   mu_hat(p)   = (1/K) sum_k M_k
   sigmaM_hat(p)= sample SD of {M_k}  (ddof=1)
   D(p)        = ( mu_hat(p) - M_char(p) ) / mu_hat(p)       (PRIMARY)

Per-prime uncertainty (from the matched null, K draws):
   Because M_char is exact and only mu_hat carries sampling noise,
     SE_D(p) = sigmaM_hat(p) / ( mu_hat(p) * sqrt(K(p)) ).
   Relative:  SE_D/D = 1 / ( |z(p)| * sqrt(K(p)) ),  where
   Per-prime significance (how many null-SD the character sits below null):
     z(p) = ( M_char(p) - mu_hat(p) ) / sigmaM_hat(p)   (expected < 0).
   z(p) is NOT reduced by K; SE_D IS. K(p) is chosen (Sec.5) so SE_D/D is
   an order of magnitude below any plausible arithmetic scatter.

Pooled decision statistic (exactly one): the log-log slope
   s_hat = weighted-LS slope of  y_i = ln D(p_i)  on  x_i = ln p_i,
   over the 30 frozen primes. Robust SE:
   sigma_s = max( formal-SE * sqrt(max(1, chi2_red)),  jackknife-SE ),
   jackknife = leave-one-prime-out. (This inflates for intrinsic
   arithmetic scatter; sigma_s ~ sigma_resid / sqrt(Sxx), Sxx below.)
Distribution under nulls: s_hat is asymptotically N(s_true, sigma_s^2);
reference s_true values are frozen in Sec.5. Confirmatory cross-checks
(NOT the primary): chi2 head-to-head of the three 1-2 param models and a
curvature coefficient (Sec.9).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. MATCHED CONTROL  (the null; must reproduce EVERY structure but the
   character's specific phase pattern)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The null must SHARE the forced Hermitian symmetry g(n-d)=conj(g(d)); a
prior wrong-null on this object omitted it and manufactured a spurious
locus (|U(b,c)| != |U(-b,c)| for the null but = for the character).

MATCHED-NULL CONSTRUCTION (per draw, seed = p * 10^6 + k, k=1..K):
 - Pairing d <-> n-d on d=1..n-1 (points P_{n-d} = -P_d = (x_d, -y_d)).
 - For each pair with d < n-d: draw phi uniform in [0,2*pi);
     g(d)   = e^{ i phi}
     g(n-d) = e^{-i phi}   (stored as the exact complex conjugate of g(d)).
 - Fixed point (only if n even, the 2-torsion point y=0, d=n/2):
     g(n/2) drawn uniform in {+1,-1} (the symmetry forces it real, exactly
     matching the character's real weight (-1)^{a_0} there).
 What it PRESERVES: |g|=1; the Hermitian symmetry (hence |U(b,c)|=|U(-b,c)|);
   the point set; the transform; the forced l2 total p^2(n-1).
 What it DESTROYS: the character's specific arithmetic phase progression
   d -> a_0 d/n. That, and only that, is what D(p) tests.

SYMMETRY CONTROL (must pass before any D is trusted, every prime, every
draw plus the character):
 (S1) By construction g(n-d) == conj(g(d)) to machine epsilon: assert
      max_d |g(n-d) - conj(g(d))| < 1e-14.
 (S2) Induced frequency symmetry: assert
      max_{b,c} | |U_g(b,c)| - |U_g(-b,c)| | < 1e-9 * sqrt(n)   (float tol),
      for the character and for a sample of null draws.
 WRONG-NULL DIAGNOSTIC (necessity demonstration, run once per prime):
   draw g' with INDEPENDENT phases on all d (no pairing). Show (a) S2 FAILS
   for g', and (b) the character measured against this wrong null shows a
   spuriously inflated deficit. This proves the Hermitian match is load-
   bearing, not decorative. (Diagnostic only; not used in the verdict.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. PLANTED (firing) CONTROL + CALIBRATION (null) CONTROL + EXACT CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------------------------
PLANTED / FIRING CONTROL (a deficit of KNOWN size the instrument must
recover; validates the D-statistic AND the SE calibration -- the thing the
whole decision rests on):
 For a fresh matched-null draw g0 with spectrum U0(b,c), define the
 injected test spectrum V_delta(b,c) = (1 - delta) * U0(b,c) for
 delta in {2e-4, 5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3}. Feed |V_delta| through the SAME
 D-statistic and z against the null ensemble.
 MUST-FIRE requirements (else the null is uninformative -- HALT):
   (P1) recovered D_hat(delta) = delta within 1*SE_D at every prime;
   (P2) monotone: D_hat strictly increases with delta;
   (P3) |z| >= 3 for delta = 1e-3 at EVERY prime (predicted |z| ~

 If the planted control does not fire, the instrument cannot size a
 deficit and NO scaling verdict may be issued.

CALIBRATION CONTROL (a target with NO deficit by construction; must return
null):
 "Null-as-test": hold out each of R=200 fresh matched-null draws and score

EXACT-ARITHMETIC CONTROL (Sec.8): at the smallest prime p=151 (n=133),
